First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x,$ treating $y$ and $z$ as constants: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{z}{\int }_{0}^{y}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y+z)\,dx\,dy\,dz & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{z}[{\int }_{0}^{y}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y+z)\,dx]dy\,dz \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{z}[-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+y+z)]_{x=0}^{x=y}\,dy\,dz \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{z}-\operatorname{cos}⁡(y+y+z)+\operatorname{cos}⁡(0+y+z)\,dy\,dz \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{z}\operatorname{cos}⁡(y+z)-\operatorname{cos}⁡(2y+z)\,dy\,dz\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $y,$ treating $z$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{z}\operatorname{cos}⁡(y+z)-\operatorname{cos}⁡(2y+z)\,dy\,dz & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}[{\int }_{0}^{z}\operatorname{cos}⁡(y+z)-\operatorname{cos}⁡(2y+z)\,dy]dz \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{[\operatorname{sin}⁡(y+z)-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2y+z)]}_{y=0}^{y=z}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(z+z)-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2z+z)-\operatorname{sin}⁡(0+z)+\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(0+z)\,dz \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2z-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡3z-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡z\,dz\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $z:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2z-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡3z-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡z\,dz & ={[-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡2z+\frac{1}{6}\operatorname{cos}⁡3z+\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡z]}_{z=0}^{z=\pi /2} \\  & =[-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi +\frac{1}{6}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{2})+\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})]-[-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡0+\frac{1}{6}\operatorname{cos}⁡0+\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡0] \\  & =[\frac{1}{2}+0+0]-[-\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{6}+\frac{1}{2}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{6} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
